stem: Let $I(k) = \int_0^1 |x^2 - k| \, dx$ for real $k$. What is the minimum value of $I(k)$?
working:
Consider the range $0 \leq x \leq 1$, let $c = \sqrt{k}$ be the crossover where $x^2 = k$. 
 For $x < c$ we have $|x^2 - k| = k - x^2$, and for $x > c$ we have $|x^2 - k| = x^2 - k$. Hence we can write $I(k)$ as $$I(k) = \int_0^c (k - x^2)\,dx + \int_c^1 (x^2 - k)\,dx$$ $$I(k)=\left[kx - \tfrac{x^3}{3}\right]_0^c + \left[\tfrac{x^3}{3} - kx\right]_c^1$$ $$I(k) = kc - \tfrac{c^3}{3} + \tfrac{1}{3} - k - \tfrac{c^3}{3} + kc$$ $$I(k) = \tfrac{4}{3}k^{3/2} - k + \tfrac{1}{3}.$$ 
 Now simply find the minimum of $I(k)$ 
 $$I'(k) = 2\sqrt{k} - 1 = 0 \Rightarrow k = \tfrac{1}{4}$$ $$I(\tfrac{1}{4}) = \tfrac{1}{6} - \tfrac{1}{4} + \tfrac{1}{3} = \tfrac{2 - 3 + 4}{12} = \boxed{\tfrac{1}{4}}$$
